subject: Accounting
title: Net Worth Analysis
description: A micro-lesson that makes Net Worth Analysis usable.

hook.text: An employee earns $60,000 a year but drives a Ferrari and owns a beach house. Something doesn't add up.

buildup.text: Net worth analysis compares a person's assets and lifestyle to their known legitimate income.

discovery.text: If assets grow faster than income can explain, the excess likely came from unreported sources.

twist.text: This method was used to convict Al Capone—the IRS proved his lifestyle exceeded his declared income.

climax.text: It requires gathering data on property, vehicles, bank accounts, and spending patterns over several years.

punchline.text: Your lifestyle tells the story your tax return won't.

quiz.question: How was net worth analysis famously used?
options: To convict Al Capone of tax evasion

details.summary: Net worth analysis is an indirect method of proving illicit income by demonstrating that a subject's wealth increased more than their known legitimate income can explain. This topic covers how forensic accountants apply this technique in tax fraud and corruption investigations.
details.whyItMatters: When criminals hide income through complex schemes, direct proof may be impossible. Net worth analysis proves the crime indirectly—spending that can't be explained by legitimate income means unreported income exists.
takeaways: Net worth analysis compares year-over-year changes in assets minus liabilities to known income sources
Unexplained increases in net worth suggest unreported income from potentially illegal sources
The IRS used this method to convict Al Capone and continues using it in tax fraud cases today

faq.question: How does net worth analysis work?
faq.answer: Calculate the subject's net worth (assets minus liabilities) at the start and end of each year. The increase in net worth, plus living expenses, minus known legitimate income, equals unexplained income. This unexplained amount constitutes evidence of hidden or illegal income.

faq.question: When is net worth analysis used in investigations?
faq.answer: It's used when direct evidence of income is unavailable—typically in tax evasion cases, corruption investigations, drug trafficking, and embezzlement. If a government employee earning $60,000 per year accumulates $2 million in assets, net worth analysis quantifies the unexplained wealth.
